title: Making a pixelart MMO RPG - looking for feedback
author: Pointline
selftext:
Hey all, long-time lurker and looking for feedback. I’m a web dev and just getting into game dev with Claude Opus 5.5. Started out as a small project and has grown to this. It’s using React, Vite for the front end and a go server. 

Assets are bought from itch.io because I was not liking what Claude was doing and instead of burning more tokens, I just tried to focus on using it for the typescript logic. The music and some of the effects are made by me in Ableton (I play guitar and keyboard so I wanted to feel like I did something lol). 

Latest feature was having the NPCs from the town controlled using TypeSafes Jev to determine which actions to take. 

It’s a bit of a mess right now, especially the lore. Going to focus on fighting scope creep and polish what is already there. 

Video was also made by Claude. 

[aetherfall.dev](https://aetherfall.dev/)

comments.author: Fluid_Equal_4942
comments.body: Can you explain the art pipeline in your project?

replies.author: Pointline
replies.body:
Yes! so it has evolved in a lot of ways and its different per asset type. The biggest breakthrough was telling Claude to build an editor for my game which allowed me to make quests, edit the tilemap, playthrough enemy bosses, change dialogue lines. For the houses I created (with Claude) a custom builder script in python that stitches the different assets together like walls, windows, pillars, roofs, and doors. I can pass the amount of previews I want generated, say 20, and then I choose which ones to keep. After that the script transform each piece into simple geometry/meshes of planes and the image gets plastered on top. This is still very much in progress and is a hit and miss. For the pixelart characters and UI/HUD it is best to use ultracode with Design in the Claude desktop app. I ask it to create a draw-off with 3-4 artist agents and make a board for each asset or idea and I give it as much reference images as possible using ChatGPT or some other AI image generator. Then its a laborious and token consuming effort of going back and forth on the attack design and movement. Because Claude is not very good at pixelart its best to take any spritesheet of a similar move or pose you want and tell it to use it as reference and this makes a significant improvement. I tried creating a pipeline using meshy for generating 3d assets, exporting to blender to rig and animate, baking the lighting but that led to more issues. One thing that really worked was asking it to create procedural animations for the characters once the pixelart was landed. I asked it to research how games like Dead Cells and RainWorld did their animations and that brought a lot of life to the characters.
